DevOps Curriculum 2026

DevOps & Infrastructure Master Guide

Master the principles of lean value streams, container orchestration, CI/CD automation pipelines, infrastructure as code, and site reliability engineering.

1. Culture & Flow ​

Establish lean management principles, optimize value streams, and cultivate high-performance organizational feedback loops across engineering teams (The DevOps Handbook, Chapters 1 & 4).

The Three Ways

Understand the foundational principles of flow, feedback, and continuous experimentation that underpin modern DevOps culture.

Value Stream Mapping

Identify bottlenecks, reduce lead times, and visualize the flow of work from code commit to production deployment.

2. Containers & Docker ​

Master containerization fundamentals, image layering, runtime isolation, and multi-container orchestration patterns (Introduction to Docker, Chapter 1; Docker Deep Dive, Chapters 2 & 5).

Container Fundamentals

Runtime Isolation

Expectation: Build lightweight container images, manage layer caching, and configure isolated network namespaces and storage volumes.

Image Architecture

Best Practices

Expectation: Write secure, multi-stage Dockerfiles that minimize attack surface and reduce overall image size for production environments.

3. CI/CD & Workflows ​

Automate building, testing, and deployment pipelines using advanced version control strategies and continuous integration frameworks (The DevOps Handbook, Chapter 9; GitHub Actions Guides).

Automated Pipelines

Continuous Integration

Expectation: Construct robust GitHub Actions workflows to execute automated testing, code linting, and rapid artifact promotion.

Advanced Git Workflows

Version Control

Expectation: Enforce clean branching strategies, pull request gating, and automated tagging to streamline collaborative feature delivery.

4. Infrastructure & SRE ​

Treat infrastructure as software through automated provisioning and scale production reliability using disciplined SRE methodologies (Infrastructure as Code, Chapters 1 & 3; Site Reliability Engineering, Chapters 3 & 5).

Infrastructure as Code

Cloud Provisioning

Expectation: Implement declarative provisioning patterns, immutability, and version-controlled infrastructure templates for cloud environments.

Site Reliability Engineering

Production Scale

Expectation: Manage service level objectives (SLOs), error budgets, and reduce operational toil through automation.

5. AI & Operations ​

Integrate artificial intelligence tools and automated machine learning workflows into modern DevOps lifecycles (AI & DevOps, Chapter 1).

AI-Driven Operations

Smart Automation

Expectation: Leverage AI assistants and predictive analytics for anomaly detection, automated log analysis, and incident triage.

6. System Foundations & Architecture ​

Understand low-level computing mechanics, hardware interfaces, and core computer architecture (Introduction to Computing Systems, Chapters 1 & 2).

Computing Systems

Low-Level Mechanics

Expectation: Comprehend the underlying machine model, instruction set architecture, and software-to-hardware execution stack.

Key Literature & Sources ​

The DevOps Handbook by Gene Kim et al. Lean management, value streams, and CI/CD (Chapters 1, 4, & 9).
Introduction to Docker by Bobby Iliev. Containerization basics and runtime mechanics (Chapter 1).
Docker Deep Dive by Nigel Poulton. Advanced container architectures and networking (Chapters 2 & 5).
Infrastructure as Code by Kief Morris. Cloud provisioning and declarative configuration (Chapters 1 & 3).
Site Reliability Engineering by Betsy Beyer et al. Reliability metrics and error budgets (Chapters 3 & 5).
AI & DevOps by Devops Shack. AI integration in deployment pipelines (Chapter 1).
Introduction to Computing Systems by Yale Patt & Sanjay Patel. Computer architecture and low-level mechanics (Chapters 1 & 2).
